fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Into a Brokerage App
fields.features_subheading: Real estate workflow automation hands the timed, repeat steps of a deal to software and keeps pricing calls with the agent.
fields.feature_1:
Write the brokerage's rules as sentences

Describe each rule the way you would tell a new agent, such as who gets a lead that arrives after 6 p.m. Emergent builds the app, its database, and its logic from that prompt.
fields.feature_2:
A response clock on every buyer lead

Set how many minutes an agent has to mark a new lead Contacted. The app sends the lead by Slack or email, and when the clock runs out it moves to the next agent in line.
fields.feature_3:
AI reads the dates in a signed contract

An AI step reads the inspection, financing, and closing dates from the signed agreement into the deal record. A date it is unsure of goes to your coordinator to confirm.
fields.feature_4:
Connects to the CRM your agents use

The app connects to any tool with an API. A new website lead lands in HubSpot, and a signed deal moves that contact to the Under Contract stage, with data synced both ways.
fields.feature_5:
One live board for every open deal

The dashboard lists every deal under contract with its next date and owner, updated live. All of it sits in a database you own, so you can pull last year's deals any time.
fields.feature_6:
The deal app's code, in your GitHub

Export the full code of the app to your GitHub repository on paid plans. Your broker or IT lead can read every routing rule and date rule before agents rely on them.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Stops on the Way to Closing
fields.tab_content_1:
A 10-minute clock moves Wren to a second agent

Wren Abernathy-Kofi asks about 418 Larkspur Lane on the Fenwick Harbor Realty website at 9:02 a.m. The app assigns him to Rhiannon Castellanos-Pike, next on the rotation. Nobody marks the lead Contacted within 10 minutes, and at 9:12 a.m. Lorcan Whitfield-Osei gets it in a Slack direct message with a Call button.
fields.tab_content_2:
Feedback forms go out one hour after each showing

Four buyers tour 418 Larkspur Lane on October 24. The app emails each showing agent a short feedback form 1 hour after the showing. Three of the 4 forms come back, and 2 say the price feels high. Imogen Tadesse-Vale, the listing agent, gets the summary by email before she calls the seller.
fields.tab_content_3:
The financing date waits for the coordinator

The seller accepts a $598,000 offer on October 27. The app reads the signed purchase agreement into the deal record: inspection by November 6, financing by November 17, closing on December 1. A handwritten change on the financing date sends it to Annika Bellweather-Moyo, the transaction coordinator, to confirm.
fields.tab_content_4:
Closing file check finds no signed repair addendum

The app checks the 418 Larkspur Lane file 5 days before the December 1 closing, against the brokerage's 16-item checklist. The file holds 15 documents, and the signed repair addendum is missing. The app marks the file Incomplete and emails Imogen Tadesse-Vale the name of the missing document.

fields.howto_title: How to Build Real Estate Workflow Automation
fields.howto_description: Seven steps that take real estate workflow automation from one closed deal to four flows your agents run on each listing.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Pull one closed deal from last quarter
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Find the system behind each record
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Set the lead rotation and its clock
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Choose the dates that get reminders
fields.howto_step_1_des: Pick a deal that closed recently and write down every step someone did by hand: the first reply to the buyer, the showing follow-ups, the dates copied off the contract, and the chase for missing paperwork. Start with the steps that follow a fixed rule.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Note where each record lives today, such as contacts in the CRM, signed contracts in the e-signature tool, and documents in shared storage. Connect each one through its API, and have the app read every record from the system that owns it.
fields.howto_step_3_des: List the agents who take new buyer leads and the order they take them in. Pick the number of minutes a lead can wait before it moves on, and decide who gets leads that arrive after hours or on weekends.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Open three recent purchase agreements and mark the dates your team tracks on each one, such as inspection, financing, and closing. Decide how many days ahead each reminder goes out, and whether it goes to the agent or the coordinator.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Turn your file review into a checklist
fields.howto_step_5_des: Ask your broker for the documents a transaction file must hold before closing, and write them as one list. Mark the ones that apply only to some deals, such as a repair addendum, so the check does not flag a file that never needed one.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Describe the workflow in one prompt
fields.howto_step_6_des: Write the rules from the last four steps as plain sentences, with the real minute counts and document names. Emergent builds the app from that prompt, down to the checklist and the dashboard.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Replay last month's leads and two open deals through the app before agents depend on it. Check that each lead reached the right agent, each reminder landed on the right day, and the file check named the right documents.
fields.hero_prompt: Build real estate workflow automation that runs on its own and logs every step.

faq_plan.q: What is real estate workflow automation?
faq_plan.a: Real estate workflow automation is the use of digital tools that replace or reduce manual tasks in a brokerage. Examples are replying to a new buyer lead, following up after a showing, or reminding an agent of a contract date. Software runs the repeat steps, and the agent keeps the client conversations and the pricing calls.

faq_plan.q: How do I set up real estate workflow automation?
faq_plan.a: Start with one closed deal and mark each step that followed a fixed rule, such as moving an unanswered lead after 10 minutes. Describe those rules in a prompt to Emergent's AI automation builder, and Emergent builds the app with its database and dashboard. Test it on a week of real leads before agents rely on it.

faq_plan.q: What should real estate workflow automation handle first?
faq_plan.a: Start with the tasks that follow a fixed rule and repeat every week, like assigning new buyer leads and sending showing follow-up. Leave pricing advice and anything the contract decides with the agent. Pick the task that slips most often in your office and build that one first.

faq_plan.q: How does real estate workflow automation keep client data private?
faq_plan.a: It limits each record to the people who need it: agents see their own deals, and the broker sees all of them. The app keeps contact details and deal documents in a database you own, and Emergent has SOC 2 Type I and ISO 27001. You would set up healthcare automation the same way, with tighter limits on patient records.

faq_plan.q: How does real estate workflow automation route leads to the right agent?
faq_plan.a: It applies your rules first, such as by listing or zip code, and puts every other lead on a rotation. The app assigns each lead, messages the agent, and passes it on when nobody marks it contacted in the minutes you choose. With no task cap, a weekend of portal leads runs the same as a quiet week.

faq_plan.q: Can real estate workflow automation read the dates in a purchase agreement?
faq_plan.a: Yes. An AI step reads the dates you name, such as inspection and closing, saves them on the deal, and sends any date it is unsure of to a person to confirm. Check each date against the contract yourself at first: a contingency is a condition written into a purchase agreement that must be met for the sale to move forward.

faq_plan.q: Can real estate workflow automation collect showing feedback?
faq_plan.a: Yes. The app emails the showing agent a few questions a set time after each showing and saves the answers on the listing, and a summary goes to the listing agent to share with the seller. You can reuse the same timed message for hotel automation, such as check-in details sent the day before arrival.

faq_plan.q: How does real estate workflow automation catch missing documents before closing?
faq_plan.a: It compares the transaction file with a checklist built from your broker's file review, a set number of days before closing, and emails the agent what is missing. Mark each document as needed on every deal or only on some. Every file stays in a database you own after the deal closes.

faq_plan.q: Can real estate workflow automation connect to the CRM my agents already use?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if the CRM has an API. Emergent builds apps that sync data in and out of any tool with an API: new leads land in the CRM, and deal stages come back to the app. Before you connect them, decide which system owns each field, such as the phone number or the deal stage.

faq_plan.q: Is real estate workflow automation the same as automating rentals?
faq_plan.a: No. This page follows a sale, from the first buyer lead to the closing file. Rentals run on leases and repair requests, which property management automation covers. A brokerage that also manages rentals can build both, since Emergent builds from a plain-English prompt and changes the app by prompting.

plan.angle: The top 10 are CRM and transaction vendors (MoxiWorks, Real Geeks, Pipedrive, Moxo, Formstack) and explainers that list real estate tasks to automate in general terms. None shows one listing moving through working screens. This page follows one listing at Fenwick Harbor Realty, 418 Larkspur Lane, through four flows: a buyer inquiry that moves to a second agent when nobody marks it contacted in 10 minutes, feedback forms sent one hour after each showing, contract dates read from the accepted purchase agreement, and a closing file check that catches one missing document. The FAQ answers the setup, lead, showing, contract-date and file questions a brokerage operator asks, keeps every legal and contract judgment with the agent and the broker, and points rentals to the property management page.
